$comment: One resource entered from two different anchored callers, which is issue #332. r.json's $recursiveRef must resolve to a.json when r is reached through a and to b.json when reached through b, and one Go type is emitted for r, so no static reading of it can be right for both. x-unmodelled is what makes that bite: dynamicScopeDecidesTheTarget does fire here -- the reach holds three anchored resources and the count says so -- and the runtime evaluator, which is the one path that could resolve the reference per value, then declines over the unmodelled keyword. Before #332 that decline dropped the schema onto the static arms and produced a type whose verdicts were false in both directions; now the document is refused, naming the reference and the keyword. TestTwoCallersRefusedWhenTheEvaluatorCannotTakeIt pins that. Beside this, two_callers_2019_modelled is the same four resources with every keyword one the evaluator models, and its four verdicts are pinned instead.
